fatal_errors: The proposed intervention omits the central AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating, atmospheric plasma spraying, and the 550 °C post-deposition anneal.
The experiment introduces irradiation and generic nuclear conditions not supported by the cited evidence or demonstrated in the target study.
The cited study concerns Cu-dependent heterogeneity in AlCrTiV0.5Cux HEAs in NaCl and does not directly establish chromium redistribution or a Cr-rich passive film in processed stainless steel.
The falsification design does not isolate the claimed mediator: thermomechanical processing may alter grain size, phase balance, residual stress, and inclusions in addition to chromium distribution.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and shares part of the governing concept with the target—protective chromium-rich passivation limiting transport and localized attack. It also proposes useful electrochemical, microscopy, and surface-chemistry measurements. However, it does not reconstruct the specific material system or intervention: an APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L annealed for 2 h at 550 °C. It misses the reported grain refinement, BCC/FCC phase structure, reduced porosity, Al/Cr-rich mixed oxide and hydroxide products, sluggish-diffusion rationale, and molten-salt hot-corrosion behavior at 900 °C. Its conditions, baseline, outcomes, and boundaries remain generic, and the supporting citation only indirectly links microstructural heterogeneity to localized corrosion. A stronger causal test would independently quantify chromium homogeneity and passive-film composition, include matched processing controls, and test whether corrosion improvement tracks the passive-film mediator after accounting for grain size, phase fraction, stress, and surface roughness.
